docs.title: $0C76 Per-Frame State Machine Cluster
docs.text:
The $0C76 cluster ($C0:0C76–$2DF0, ~8,600 bytes, 20+ blocks) is the per-frame state machine that drives door and switch tile-opening animations on the map. Sub_0C76 runs every frame from GameLoop_FrameBody; it dispatches to mode handlers (ModeE6/EC/EE/FA/FC) that advance a $7E:3000 tile table, compute VRAM write indices corner-by-corner, and trigger SPC audio cues. DefaultHandler covers the non-opening steady state. Sub_18D9 and its callees manage the full scene transition sequence triggered by the mode-dispatch path.

Session 19: ModeE6_Handler + Sub_1B36 + Sub_1B90 + Sub_2824 + Sub_19C7 = 379 bytes. Session 20: ModeEC_Handler + ModeEE_Handler + ModeFA_Handler + ModeFC_Handler = 2173 bytes. Session 21: DefaultHandler + Sub_1BA7 = 513 bytes. Mode-dispatch closure confirmed. Session 22: Sub_18D9 (172 B) + Sub_1985 (66 B) + Sub_1ADF (87 B) = 325 bytes. Screen-transition subsystem closed. Session 23: Sub_011B (138 B) + Sub_01A5 (167 B) + Sub_0905 (19 B) + Sub_0918 (19 B) + Sub_1A03 (169 B) + Sub_B192 (30 B) + Sub_E935 (29 B) = 571 bytes. Scene context save/restore path closed. Session 24: Sub_595C (33 B) + Sub_597D (92 B) = 125 bytes. Scene entity dispatcher pair closed; Sub_E12A scoped at 1034 bytes own body + ~1336 byte callee cluster → deferred. Session 25: Sub_E12A (1034 B) = 1034 bytes. Head routine of the Sub_E12A cluster matched. Callees Sub_E534 and Sub_E687 identified. Session 26: Sub_E534 (339 B) + Sub_E687 (178 B) + Sub_E739 (131 B) + Sub_E7BC (131 B) + Sub_E83F (131 B) + Sub_E8C2 (115 B) = 1025 bytes. Sub_E12A cluster COMPLETE (7 routines, 2059 bytes across sessions 25–26). Session 27: Sub_E952 (40 B) + Sub_E97A (48 B) + Sub_E9AA (56 B) = 144 bytes. Sprite slot allocation cluster matched (single/dual/triple variants). ASAR_QUIRKS.md updated with db $A9,$7F trick. Sub_E12A caller audit: 2 callers found ($C0:0212 in Sub_01A5, $C0:47E9 in uncharted area). Session 28: Sub_CB3A (162 B) = 162 bytes. Animation-frame gate for sprite-slot init cluster matched. Scoped the full $CB3A–$D800 sprite-slot init cluster: 9+ routines sharing a common template (JSR Sub_CB3A → slot alloc → 16/32-tile DMA loop → OAM staging). Cluster table added to BANK_MAP.md. Session 29: Sub_CBDC (492 B) + Sub_CDC8 (301 B) + Sub_CEF5 (559 B) + Sub_D28A (131 B) + Sub_D30D (490 B) = 1973 bytes. Sprite-slot init cluster body matched: single-slot gated, single-slot OAM-only, complex dual-slot dispatch, dual-slot first-pass, dual-slot second-pass. Session 30: Updated progress denominators to code-only baseline (359,278 bytes code vs 4 MB ROM). Added bank code-density table to BANK_MAP.md. Sub_D4F7 (273 B) + Sub_D608 (131 B) = 404 bytes. Triple-slot dispatch matched; Sub_D546 (pass-0 non-$68 body) is a BRA-entered tail inside Sub_D4F7. Sub_D608 (pass-0 $68 variant) is a separate named routine. Pass-1 and pass-2+ variants (Sub_D68B, Sub_D738, Sub_D7E5, Sub_DA69) remain unmatched. Session 31: Sub_D68B (173 B) + Sub_D738 (173 B) + Sub_D7E5 (644 B) + Sub_DA69 (703 B) = 1,693 bytes. All four triple-slot pass-1 and pass-2+ variants matched. Key insight: pass-1 variants use SEP #$30 and LDX $6D reload; pass-2+ variants use SEP #$10 before OAM staging (A stays 16-bit for slot arithmetic). X-position layout differs: non-$68 (Sub_D7E5) has 8+gap+4 entries; $68 (Sub_DA69) has 4+gap+8. Sprite-slot init cluster COMPLETE (12 routines, 4,232 bytes, $CB3A–$DD27, sessions 28–31). Session 32: Sub_CB0A (48 B) + Sub_D124 (358 B) + Sub_DD28 (1,026 B) = 1,432 bytes. Dispatcher layer above the sprite-slot init cluster matched. Sub_CB0A is the top-level sprite-type router (bits 0-1 of $1201,X → CDC8/D124/DD28). Sub_D124 is the 8-slot OAM-staging path (type 1, Y=$40, reads from WRAM $001700 table). Sub_DD28 is the 12-slot OAM-staging path (type 2, Y=$60, two sub-paths on $0D00,X==$68 for different X-position layouts). All three are OAM-only (no VRAM DMA). Extended matched region: $CB0A–$E129. Session 33: Obj_AnimTickAndQueue (236 B) + Field_ProcessAnimQueue (99 B) + Obj_BuildSpriteFrameStep (49 B) = 384 bytes. Closed the $C98A–$CB09 residual gap adjacent to the sprite-slot system. Obj_AnimTickAndQueue arbitrates focus slots $76/$77, ticks animation timers, and reads frame-step bytes from bank $E4; Field_ProcessAnimQueue is the VBlank-gated queue processor (reads SLHV/OPVCT scanline position); Obj_BuildSpriteFrameStep is the per-slot frame-build dispatcher. Bank $C1 scouted: 481 named routines, full battle engine (63,904 bytes, 97% code density); entry points Battle_Mul8/Battle_MulAccum/Battle_Divide at $C1:0089–$C1:010C are the recommended session 34 start.

Session 34: Battle_Mul8 (30 B) + Battle_MulAccum (48 B) + Battle_Divide (54 B) + shift helpers (18 B) = 150 bytes. Opened Bank $C1 (battle engine). Math utility cluster complete at $C1:0089–$C1:011E. Caller audit: Battle_Mul8 called from 11 sites, Battle_MulAccum from 13, Battle_Divide from 13, ShiftCluster from 3. Session 35: BattleMsg_FormatNumberDigits (85 B) + Battle_DivTen9499 (53 B) + BattleMsg_ReencodeTextBuffer (80 B) + Battle_SinLookup (41 B) + Calc_Delta16 (119 B) = 378 bytes. Number-display cluster ($C1:011F–$C1:01F8) + trig/geometry cluster ($C1:01F9–$C1:0298). New M=0-entry convention for formatting routines (caller sets REP #$20). Battle_SinLookup uses $C0F900 sine table. Calc_Delta16 uses $C0F300 direction-angle table. Session 36: BattleUI_BuildStatusBarFrame (782 B) + BattleMsg_BlankLeadingZeros (32 B) = 814 bytes. Status-bar UI cluster entry matched. BuildStatusBarFrame is the largest single routine so far: clears and rebuilds the entire battle status tilemap ($0CC0) on each full-refresh call, with three layout variants (BattleGaugeDisplayType $9F20) and inner loops for PC name tiles, HP/MaxHP/MP digit formatting, ATB/TP gauge tiles, and enemy name tiles. BattleMsg_BlankLeadingZeros is the 32-byte leading-zero suppressor (blanks hundreds/tens digit if == $73 zero-glyph). Stubs added for four not-yet-matched callees: BattleUI_DrawSlotGaugeBar ($C106F0), BattleMenu_DrawReadyWindowEdges ($C1081E), BattleSys_SlotPanelRefresh ($C10785), BattleUI_SetPanelAttrColumn ($C108E8). ASAR_QUIRKS.md updated with the SBC/ADC 16-bit immediate encoding quirk (db $E9/$69 workaround). Confirmed db $E9,$xx,$00 / db $69,$xx,$00 pattern is needed for all SBC/ADC.w #$NNNN in M=0 context.

Session 39: BattleMenu_RenderItemListRows (83 B) + BattleMenu_RenderItemRow (216 B) + BattleMenu_RenderTechListRows (75 B) + BattleMenu_BuildTechAvailFlags (56 B) + BattleMenu_RenderTechRow (171 B) + CODE_JP_C10BB6 (29 B) + BattleMenu_BlankMpCostDigits (45 B) + CODE_JP_C10C00 (45 B) = 720 bytes. Battle menu item/tech list rendering cluster ($C1:095D–$C1:0C2C). Key techniques: MVN $7E,$CC for 11-byte name copies from ROM; per-PC usability table AND.l $CCF9FB,X for item attribute selection; dead RTS byte ($60) at $0BB5 reproduced exactly; all ADC #imm in M=0 context via db $69 trick. disasm.py X-width fix (session 38) confirmed correct — spot-checks at $010D and $0089 look clean.

Session 40: BattleMenu_UpdateWindows (28 B) + BattleMenu_UpdateMainWindow (58 B) + BattleMenu_UpdateTechWindow (471 B) + BattleMenu_DrawTechCursorRow (96 B) + BattleMenu_ClearTechCursorTiles (39 B) + BattleMenu_UpdateTechMpAvail (349 B) + BattleSys_SlotMenuReadyPredicate (16 B) + BattleMenu_LoadCommandWindowMap (16 B) = 1,073 bytes. Per-frame window upkeep cluster ($C1:0C2D–$C1:104D + $C1:1C3A–$C1:1C49). Architecture: UpdateWindows is the top-level dispatcher; UpdateMainWindow ties back to the already-matched status-bar cluster ($C10299, $C105A7, $C10872); UpdateTechWindow is the largest new routine (471 B) — copies text buffer, composes border from $CCFA95 template, fills MP digit cells, resolves cursor slot, falls through to DrawTechCursorRow. UpdateTechMpAvail is a 349-byte per-row MP affordability sweep. KEY: CODE_JP_C1103D (shared exit RTS at $103D) jumped to from 3 separate routines — needs global label. New global-label pattern used throughout to avoid asar scope-reset issue (asar quirk #6).

Session 41: BattleMenu_RefreshIfDirtyL (23 B) + BattleMenu_RefreshIfDirtyAndTick (27 B) + BattleMenu_DrawCursorSprites (62 B) = 112 bytes. Matched the outer dirty-flag gate pair that sits above the window-upkeep cluster: RefreshIfDirtyL is the JSL-entry twin reached via the cross-bank vector at $C10012, RefreshIfDirtyAndTick is its same-bank JSR sibling (adds a per-frame service tick via JSL $CD0009). Both share an identical rebuild chain: DequeueReadyBattler -> UpdateWindows -> ProcessInput -> UpdateCursorOverlay (three stub labels added for the latter three, not yet matched). DrawCursorSprites is a small adjacent routine (called from inside ProcessInput) that builds the 4-tile OAM cursor sprite from a ROM template. Also fixed a docs-staleness bug this session: PROGRESS.md's own Bank $C0 heading had drifted 384 bytes stale, and tools/progress.py couldn't parse comma-formatted byte counts, silently dropping Bank $C1 from the generated homepage snippet — both fixed.

Session 41 (continued): BattleMenu_ProcessInput (142 B) + BattleMenu_CycleActivePcPrev (55 B) + BattleMenu_CycleActivePcNext (56 B) + BattleMenu_CursorUp (20 B) + BattleMenu_CursorDown (23 B) + Battle_ZeroResultEE (5 B) + Battle_StopSfx (18 B) = 319 bytes. Closed the command-window input-handling cluster: ProcessInput is the per-frame dispatcher, polling two pad-edge bytes ($EE buttons, $EF D-pad) and routing to submenu handlers (tech/item/target-select, all left as stub labels) or to the main-menu cursor-move/PC-cycle/confirm routines matched here. CycleActivePcPrev/Next and CursorUp/Down are small, symmetric leaf routines; Battle_ZeroResultEE and Battle_StopSfx are shared tails pulled in from elsewhere in the bank ($179C and $1B55 respectively — not contiguous with the rest of the cluster, added as their own regions). One curiosity: both CycleActivePc routines have a branch on $A0D4 (cursor-position-save setting) that the reference disassembly marks unreachable in shipped code; reproduced byte-exact regardless since correctness here means matching the ROM, not judging live reachability. BattleMenu_ConfirmCommand (the confirm-dispatch entry, itself leading into three big per-row command-execution branches) was deliberately left as a stub — clearly a separate, much larger session's worth of work.

Session 41 (continued again): BattleMenu_ConfirmCommand (33 B) + BattleMenu_ChooseAttack (32 B) + BattleMenu_OpenTechList (49 B) + BattleMenu_OpenItemList (51 B) = 165 bytes. Matched the confirm-button dispatcher and its three immediate row handlers. ConfirmCommand reads the active PC's menu cursor row and tail-jumps to whichever row was confirmed; ChooseAttack (row 0) jumps straight into target-select mode via a new stub, BattleMenu_BuildTargetList; OpenTechList/OpenItemList (rows 1/2) just flip the submenu type and render the corresponding list, deferring the actual list navigation to the still-stubbed TechListInput/ItemListInput. This closes the top-level confirm dispatch — the remaining unmatched code in this neighborhood is entirely inside the three submenu input handlers and the targeting subsystem, each a substantial cluster of its own.

Session 41 (continued yet again): BattleMenu_BuildTargetList (100 B). Matched the target-list initializer called by ChooseAttack (and, per the reference disassembly, the still-unmatched tech/item confirm paths too) — resets target-selection state, blanks two 11-entry lists to $FF, snapshots the submenu type for cancel-to-return, then dispatches through a raw jump table at $C11FF8 keyed by a clamped $960D target mode. That jump table and everything it points to (a dozen-plus BattleTgt_* handlers implementing per-mode target collection, e.g. "all enemies," "single enemy," "all allies") is a large, self-contained targeting subsystem left fully unmatched — referenced only by raw address (JSR ($1FF8,X)), the same pattern already used for the bank $C0 $5D6E dispatch table. One bug caught during matching: an early draft nested LDA #$FF inside the clear-loop instead of before it, which produced a working-but-wrong branch target (make diff caught it immediately as a 1-byte mismatch at $C1:1F9C).

Session 41 (fifth increment): BattleMenu_DequeueReadyBattler (67 B). Matched the last remaining stub callee of the menu dirty-flag gates from earlier today. Pops the head of a small ATB-ready queue ($95D6-$95D9, 3 deep, count in $95DA) into the active menu roster, restoring that battler's saved cursor position and taking over as active PC if none was already set. Reproduced one small original-code quirk exactly: the queue-shift step reads $95D8 twice (into both $95D7 and $95D9) rather than reading $95D9 for the second copy — almost certainly harmless since the live queue count never exceeds what the shift correctly updates, but reproduced as-is rather than "corrected," per the project's byte-exact-first philosophy.

Session 41 (sixth increment): BattleMenu_RemoveBattlerFromReady (144 B). Matched service 2 of the cross-bank $C10045 service API — the inverse of DequeueReadyBattler, removing a battler from the menu-ready state whether it's currently queued or already the active menu PC. If it was the displayed active PC, this cancels any open submenu/targeting state and searches for another valid roster slot to promote (or clears the active-PC entirely if none remain). Hit the exact same class of bug as BuildTargetList earlier today: an early draft nested a one-time LDA $80 inside the queue-scan loop instead of before it, shifting the loop's branch target by one byte; caught immediately by make diff as a single-byte mismatch on the branch's own offset byte. Two occurrences of the identical mistake in one session was enough to write it up as a standing note for next time (see the project's session notes / CLAUDE.md-adjacent guidance): a lone 1-byte make diff mismatch landing on a branch operand near a loop is a strong signal the loop label is one instruction too early.

Session 41 (seventh increment): BattleMenu_TargetSelectInput (185 B). Matched the per-frame input handler for target-select mode — the third and last of the three submenu-input stubs to fall this session (TechListInput and ItemListInput remain). Notable find: an 18-byte block of genuinely dead code at $115B6-$115C7, a near-duplicate of the item-graphic copy loop just above it, except its loop-continue branch targets unrelated code further down instead of looping back on itself — meaning it can only ever execute one iteration if reached at all, and in fact nothing in the routine's control flow reaches it (both live paths branch past it via BRA). Reproduced byte-exact as orphaned/unreachable bytes rather than omitted, consistent with the project's standing approach to dead code (cf. session 39's dead RTS byte, session 41's earlier $A0D4 "unreachable per reference" branches). This is the first genuinely dead multi-instruction block found in Bank $C1, as opposed to a single stray byte.

Session 41 (eighth and final increment): BattleMenu_CommitAction (308 B) + BattleMenu_ConsumePartnerSlot (30 B) + BattleMenu_TargetNext (26 B) + BattleMenu_TargetPrev (22 B) = 386 bytes. This is the routine every confirm path in the whole menu-input neighborhood ultimately reaches: it builds an 8-byte command record ($93EE+, indexed via a $CCFAF0 slot->sprite lookup already seen in ConsumePartnerSlot) encoding action type, target, and tech/item id, handles dual/triple-tech partner consumption (a second battler gets "used up" alongside the caster for combo techs), decrements item stock, and hands off active-PC focus to the next ready battler using the same roster-scan tail as RemoveBattlerFromReady. TargetNext/TargetPrev are small D-pad cycling helpers for the target cursor, structurally identical to CycleActivePcPrev/Next from earlier today. This closes the entire $C1:161A–$C1:179B span, connecting directly into the already-matched Battle_ZeroResultEE — the whole neighborhood from the menu dirty-flag gate ($10E3) through target confirmation is now one continuous matched region apart from three remaining stubs.

Session 41 (ninth increment, new day): BattleMenu_TechListInput (73 B) + BattleMenu_TechConfirm (38 B) + BattleMenu_TechListCancel (30 B) + BattleMenu_TechListPrev (71 B) + BattleMenu_TechListNext (73 B) = 285 bytes. Closes the entire tech-list-input stub. TechListInput is the per-frame dispatcher; TechConfirm hands off to targeting the same way ChooseAttack does; TechListCancel restores the saved cursor/scroll and returns to the main menu; TechListPrev/Next are the interesting pair — moving the tech cursor isn't a simple increment/decrement, because unavailable techs (per-slot availability byte $1CDB) must be skipped, and skipping can require the visible window to scroll. Both routines walk step-by-step to the next/previous available entry, then replay that same step count against the (cursor row, scroll offset) pair to keep the two in sync, scrolling a row at a time whenever the row would go out of the visible 0-2 range. Closes the entire tech submenu now that item is the only list-input handler left as a stub.

Session 41 (tenth and final increment): BattleMenu_ItemListInput (91 B) + BattleMenu_ItemConfirm (67 B) + BattleMenu_ItemListCancel (17 B) + BattleMenu_ItemCursorUp (22 B) + BattleMenu_ItemCursorDown (26 B) + BattleMenu_ItemListPageDown (27 B) + BattleMenu_ItemListPageUp (20 B) + BattleMenu_ItemListRefresh (22 B) + BattleMenu_ItemListScrollUp (30 B) + BattleMenu_ItemListScrollDown (30 B) = 352 bytes. Closes the entire item submenu — and with it, every submenu-input handler in the whole command-menu subsystem (main/tech/item/target-select) is now matched. Architecturally simpler than the tech list: items have no per-slot "unavailable, skip it" flag during cursor movement, so up/down just move the cursor and call a scroll helper at the row-0/row-2 edges. Two implementation details worth flagging: (1) BattleMenu_ItemListScrollUp has a genuinely odd redundant double-branch — two consecutive BEQs testing the same unchanged zero flag, where the second one's target can never actually be reached, since getting there at all requires the first check to have already found the flag clear; reproduced exactly. (2) BattleMenu_ItemListPageDown/PageUp don't call the render routine directly — they JSR into a sub-entry point inside ItemListScrollDown/ScrollUp (the exact address of the internal JSR BattleMenu_RenderItemListRows instruction), reusing that shared render+indicator-invalidate tail rather than duplicating it. Required exposing that entry point as a real global label rather than a local .dot label, per the project's known asar quirk #6 (a new global label resets local-label scope, so a label referenced from a different routine's scope can't be local). Also corrected two stale/incorrect inline comments in session 39's BattleMenu_RenderItemRow — $1580,X/$1583,X were mislabeled "unconfirmed-animation flag" and "item ID" respectively; BattleMenu_ItemConfirm's clear indexing this session ($1580=id, $1583=quantity) made the error obvious.

Session 42: BattleMenu_UpdateCursorOverlay (828 B) — the last stub in the command-menu neighborhood, now matched; $C1:1320–$C1:1B18 is one continuous matched span. A four-way per-frame dispatcher: no active PC (hide cursor), tech list (single cursor, or a 2–3 sprite cluster over the caster plus dual/triple-tech partners decoded from the nibble-packed $9EE7), item list (scroll-arrow glow + row-highlight quad, each cached against its last-drawn value so a VRAM upload is only queued when something changed; down arrow uses attr $A9 vs the up arrow's $29), and target select (single cursor with an enemy info-panel dispatch through two cross-bank message vectors, or a multi-target sweep that draws 3 selection-list entries per frame into the 4 available cursor OAM slots and resumes next frame from $960B, wrapping after 6 — i.e. cursors alternate between target groups across frames). The battler-screen-position idiom ($1D0C,X/$1D23,X base + $9708,X/$9713,X live offset − $10) appears six times, always inlined.

Session 43: BattleMenu_EnqueueReadyBattler (60 B, service 1 of the $C10045 API — the counterpart of DequeueReadyBattler) + the whole target-mode handler layer: BattleTgt_RunAreaQuery (service 7, 27 B incl. its table), BattleTgt_ModeTable (66 B), 18 handlers (760 B) and 6 candidate-list helpers (120 B) = 1,033 bytes. The simple modes are slot-range presets into one shared list builder (CollectValidTargets); KO'd, self and specific-party-member modes are bespoke; the area modes all anchor on the caster / an aimed enemy / a party member found by id, fill the $9604–$9608 parameter block, call one of four still-unmatched geometry routines (now label stubs) and select the whole result. Service 7 exposes the same geometry routines to code outside the bank. Also corrected ConsumePartnerSlot's $93EE comments: bit 7 = waiting for command (set by EnqueueReadyBattler), bit 6 = command queued. Verification upgrade: rebuilt over a ROM copy with the new ranges zeroed to prove all 1,033 bytes come from source.

Progress so far: Sub_E12A cluster COMPLETE. Sprite-slot init cluster ($CB3A–$DD27, 12 routines) COMPLETE. Dispatcher layer (Sub_CB0A, Sub_D124, Sub_DD28, $CB0A–$E129) COMPLETE. Animation tick/queue cluster ($C98A–$CB09) COMPLETE. Bank $C1 opened (sessions 34–41): math utilities + number-display cluster + trig/geometry cluster + status-bar UI cluster + item/tech list rendering cluster + window upkeep cluster + menu dirty-flag gate + cursor sprite builder + command-window input-handling cluster + confirm dispatch + target-list initializer + ready-battler dequeue/remove pair + target-select input + command-commit cluster + tech-list input cluster + item-list input cluster + cursor overlay + ready-queue enqueue + target-mode handler layer. 8,061 of 63,904 Bank $C1 bytes matched (12.61%). The entire battle command-menu subsystem — dirty-flag gate through all three submenus through target confirmation through command commit, plus the per-frame cursor overlay — is now matched. The BattleTgt_* target-mode layer behind $C11FF8 is matched too (session 43); only its four area-geometry routines ($C1:2332–$C1:27C4) remain.

Mode handler progression (all confirmed byte-exact): | Handler | Addr | Bytes | Mode-table updates | VRAM passes | dp:$60 | Direction | |---------|------|-------|--------------------|-------------|--------|-----------| | ModeE6_Handler | $0D78 | 231 | 2 | 2×4 = 8 | 0 (STZ) | row+ | | ModeEC_Handler | $0E5F | 437 | 4 | 4×4 = 16 | $01 | row+, col- | | ModeEE_Handler | $1014 | 437 | 4 | 4×4 = 16 | $01 | row-, col- | | ModeFA_Handler | $11C9 | 651 | 6 | 6×4 = 24 | $02 | row+, 3-col | | ModeFC_Handler | $1454 | 648 | 6 | 6×4 = 24 | $02 | row-, 3-col | | DefaultHandler | $16DC | 509 | conditional | bit-1 + bit-5 loop + bit-0 swap | — | dp:$5D/$5E |

Next: the four area-geometry routines BattleTgt_Area2332 / Area23A4 / Area25A3 / Area2701 ($C1:2332–$C1:27C4, ~1.1 KB, currently label stubs) — matching them closes the targeting system end to end.
